subject: OrchidPay performance follow-up — parallel channels & quota proposal
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
To: Alex Kim <alex.kim@orchidpay.com>
Cc: Riya Patel <riya.patel@orchidpay.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 23 Mar 2028 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Orchi dPay performance follow-up — parallel channels & quota proposal

Hi Alex / Riya —

Great to meet earlier. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can size a clean pilot:

1) Targets you mentioned during the call
   - P95 generation latency target: <= 300 ms (95% of requests)
   - Peak sustained parallel request volume: ~600 parallel in steady state with spikes to ~1,000 for short windows
   - Streaming sessions (WebSocket multiplexed): ~150 concurrent; 200 peak
   - Daily token budget (estimate): ~1.2M tokens/day

2) Clarifications we need to firm pricing and quota proposal:
   - Are the 600 parallel requests independent user sessions or multiplexed through a smaller set of connections?
   - Typical sequence length / prompt + response average tokens? (you said ~120 tokens earlier — confirm)
   - Which endpoints will be streaming vs simple generation, and the expected split during peak?

3) Next steps we propose
   - Alex to confirm answers above by Monday (3/27)
   - Redwood will produce a first-pass quota + MAP and a recommended connection strategy (multiplexing vs persistent pools)
   - Schedule a short follow-up to review technical constraints and cost tradeoffs (30 min)

I'm looping in Ben and Laura from Capacity & Pricing to propose concrete numbers. We'll attach a draft MAP and a worksheet for you to validate.

Thanks —
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
--
Attachment: orchidpay_map_draft.pdf (1 page)

From: Alex Kim <alex.kim@orchidpay.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Cc: Riya Patel <riya.patel@orchidpay.com>, Sam Torres <sam.torres@orchidpay.com>
Date: Thu, 23 Mar 2028 13:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Orchi dPay performance follow-up — parallel channels & quota proposal

Thanks Hannah — quick answers inline:

- Parallel requests: the 600 steady is effectively 600 active user requests (each usually maps to a distinct HTTP request). We do multiplex a subset of long-lived devices (mobile app) through a connection broker, but most desktop/web clients open their own request per message. Spikes to ~1,000 happen during payroll cutovers (approx 3–5 minute windows).
- Avg tokens: when we include context + response we're at ~140 tokens median; heavy financial digests push to 400 tokens occasionally (~5% of requests).
- Streaming: about 30% of requests during normal flow are streaming (primarily incremental receipts and real-time guidance). At peak that ratio can rise to ~45%.

Other constraints:
- We prefer to keep long-lived WebSocket connections (multiplexing many logical sessions) to reduce TLS churn.
- Security: we will need audit logs for calls and a SOC2 attestation for any dedicated lanes.

I'll confirm numbers formally by 3/27 and attach an internal traffic matrix.

—Alex
Alex Kim
Head of Platform Engineering, OrchidPay

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Kim <alex.kim@orchidpay.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 24 Mar 2028 09:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Redwood initial quota proposal / comments on multiplexing

Alex — thanks for the quick clarifications. Based on the traffic profile you provided, here is a conservative first-pass from Pricing & Capacity: 

Proposal summary (hosted plan pilot):
- Parallel request quota: 800 concurrent request tokens (covers 600 steady + 200 buffer for spikes)
- Streaming session quota: 250 concurrent streaming sessions (covers 200 peak + buffer for handoffs)
- Connection pool guidance: allow ~250 persistent TLS connections for your integration (we recommend multiplexing logical sessions over these connections where possible to reduce socket churn)
- Token throughput cap: soft limit at 90,000 tokens/minute with burst up to 130,000 tokens/minute (billing applies to actual tokens)
- Latency: we'll target p95 <= 300 ms on the suggested model family under the pilot traffic pattern; final SLA requires Dedicated reservation

Notes on constraints and tradeoffs:
- On hosted accounts we default to a 100 persistent connections limit per account to protect noisy neighbors. For this pilot we can temporarily raise that to 250 under an agreed MAP and traffic shaping rules.
- Multiplexing logical sessions over fewer connections reduces TLS overhead but increases per-connection buffer (KV cache) pressure in the runtime — we will instrument to ensure tail latencies stay within your target.
- If you need hard SLOs (financially-backed SLA) or larger guaranteed baseline throughput, Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) will be the right next step; we can draft a Dedicated sizing based on your traffic matrix.

Attached: redwood_quota_worksheet.xlsx (worksheet where you can input daily/hourly patterns). I've added suggested cost bands for the pilot vs dedicated.

Next steps we recommend:
- Alex/Riya: confirm the traffic matrix + token averages by 3/27 (if you can upload to the Drive link in the MAP)
- Redwood: finalize MAP & a short test plan to validate latency under a realistic multiplexing pattern
- Schedule a 30-min sync (proposed 3/29 or 3/30) to lock numbers and discuss procurement cadence

Happy to jump on a call to walk through the worksheet.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Head of Capacity & Pricing, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_quota_worksheet.xlsx (Excel, 3 sheets)

Ben / Hannah — thanks, this is helpful. A couple quick commercial questions from procurement before we sign up for the pilot:

- Estimated incremental monthly cost for the proposed hosted pilot quotas (800 parallel, 250 streaming). Can you provide a ballpark range?
- If we test multiplexing heavily during the pilot and decide not to migrate to Dedicated, will Redwood keep the raised connection pool (250) or revert to defaults?
- Timeline: how long to lift the pool limit and apply the pilot quotas once we give the thumbs up?

Also cc'ing our procurement lead (Riya) to coordinate PO timing.

—Sam
Sam Torres
CTO, OrchidPay

Date: Fri, 30 Mar 2028 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Orchi dPay performance follow-up — parallel channels & quota proposal

Sam / Team — quick answers and next steps: 

- Ballpark cost: for the pilot profile above we estimate $12k–$19k / month on hosted (range accounts for token consumption variability and streaming session runtime). We'll include a clearer line-item estimate in the MAP draft.
- Connection pool behavior: for pilots we can temporarily raise the persistent connection limit to 250 for a 30-day trial window; unless you request an extension, the account will revert to default limits after the trial. If you move to Dedicated, the limits are configurable per-reservation.
- Timeline: once we receive confirmed traffic matrix + PO intent we can lift limits and enable quotas within 48 business hours (subject to some operational checks).

Proposed immediate actions:
1) Alex / Riya: upload your traffic matrix to the Drive link by EOD Monday 3/27.
2) Sam / Riya: indicate which cost band you'd prefer to explore (pilot only vs pilot + Dedicated evaluation).
3) I will schedule a 30-min technical sync for 3/29 (tentative) to walk test plan and acceptance criteria.

If this looks good I will finalize the MAP and circulate a version for signatures.

Thanks —
Hannah
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
